summary_paragraph: The patient, a woman with T1-T2 paraplegia and a history of recurrent pneumonia and UTIs, was admitted after experiencing vomiting, lethargy, and respiratory failure following clonazepam use. She was found to have hypercarbic respiratory failure requiring intubation, right lower lobe aspiration pneumonia, and a Proteus mirabilis urinary tract infection. She developed septic shock requiring pressors briefly and was treated with vancomycin and meropenem. Her mental status improved as sedative effects resolved and infection was controlled. She was extubated on hospital day 7 and transitioned to 3L oxygen. Chronic issues including COPD, neuropathic pain, and swallowing difficulties were addressed, with plans for speech therapy and pain management follow-up. She was discharged home with services in stable condition.
